title: Honey Glazed Mushrooms
description: Honey Glazed Mushrooms are a glossy Chinese-style appetizer or side dish featuring golden-seared mushrooms coated in a sweet, savory, tangy glaze. Fragrant garlic and ginger combine with honey, soy sauce, oyster sauce, and rice vinegar, while sesame oil adds a rich aromatic finish.

ingredients.title: For the Mushrooms
items: Button mushrooms – 250 g, cleaned and trimmed

instruction.title: Step 1 – Preparing the Mushrooms
steps: Clean and trim the mushrooms thoroughly.
Slice large mushrooms into bite-sized pieces, while small mushrooms can be left whole.
Pat the mushrooms completely dry to ensure they sear rather than steam.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Searing the Mushrooms
steps: Heat a wok or heavy-bottomed skillet over high heat.
Add the vegetable or peanut oil and heat until hot but not smoking.
Add the mushrooms and stir-fry for 3–4 minutes until they begin to turn golden.
Avoid overcrowding the pan; cook in batches if necessary.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Adding the Aromatics
steps: Stir-fry for 30–45 seconds until fragrant, taking care not to burn them.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Preparing the Honey Glaze
steps: In a small bowl, combine honey, light soy sauce, oyster sauce, rice vinegar, and white pepper.
Pour the glaze over the mushrooms.
Toss thoroughly to coat the mushrooms evenly.
Cook for another 2–3 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly and becomes glossy.

instruction.title: Step 5 – Finishing & Garnishing
steps: Drizzle sesame oil over the glazed mushrooms.
Give the mushrooms a final quick toss.
Garnish with sliced spring onions and toasted sesame seeds if using.

instruction.title: Step 6 – Serving
steps: Serve hot as an appetizer or side dish.
Alternatively, spoon the mushrooms over steamed rice for a satisfying vegetarian main course.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve hot as a Chinese-style appetizer or side dish.
Spoon over steamed jasmine rice for a simple vegetarian main course.
Pair with fried rice, noodles, or other Chinese stir-fried dishes.

chefTips: Use a heavy-bottomed wok or skillet to maintain even heat and achieve a deep golden sear.
Do not overcrowd the pan, as mushrooms release moisture and can steam instead of browning.
Adjust the honey according to the natural sweetness of the mushrooms; the finished glaze should be balanced rather than overly sweet.
For extra depth, add a small splash of Shaoxing wine during the glazing stage.
Pat mushrooms thoroughly dry before cooking to maximize browning and prevent excess water from diluting the glaze.
Add sesame oil only at the end to preserve its delicate aroma.
